WHAT I IMPLEMENTED MYSELF
- Greedy mesher (packages/client/src/mesher/**): 0fps-style slice sweep over 16^3 sections, reading an 18^3 padded copy (PADDED, paddedIndex from core-types) so neighbour faces and cross-section light resolve without touching other chunks. Per-axis masks merge runs into quads; AO = 3 - (side1 + side2 + corner) per corner with quad-split flipping when ao(0,0) + ao(1,1) > ao(0,1) + ao(1,0); vertices are Uint16 interleaved at VERTEX_STRIDE_U16 = 8 in VERTEX_LANE order (PosX, PosY, PosZ, Reserved, TexLayer, NormalAo, Light, Tint); Opaque, Cutout and Translucent are emitted as three separate MeshBuffers (RENDER_LAYER) so depth writes and sorting differ per layer. Positions are in 1/16 block units and the shader divides by 16. MESHER_VERSION = 1, MAX_VERTICES = 65532 for Uint16 index safety.
- Appearance/texture tables (mesher/appearance.ts, mesher/textures.ts): the client owns the canonical TEXTURE_NAMES list (73 entries, index 0 is the missing tile); lane 4 stores that index, which is also the array-texture layer. Water, ice and glass are full cubes; SNOW_BLOCK reuses the snow tile; doors, snow_layer and pistons are cube approximations for now; grass, foliage, water and lava use TINT slots (TINT_COUNT = 5) resolved in the shader instead of baked vertex colours.
- Worker protocol (packages/client/src/worker/**): MesherMessage / MesherResponse with revision matching (stale responses dropped), ArrayBuffer transfer of the interleaved and index buffers, a static new Worker(new URL('./mesher.worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' }) so Vite can bundle it, a local worker-env.d.ts so worker globals do not collide with DOM types, an inline fallback when Worker is unavailable (used by the E2E test mode), and crossOriginIsolated feature detection instead of requiring SharedArrayBuffer.
- three.js renderer (packages/client/src/render/**): WebGL2, a 2D array texture built from the assets-gen atlas layers, one ShaderMaterial per render layer (defines CUTOUT / TRANSLUCENT), frustum culling over per-section bounds, render distance, a day/night cycle driving uSunDir / uSunColor / uAmbient, fog and an underwater tint via uUnderwater. Uploads are throttled to PERF.uploadsPerFrame; RenderStats reports drawCalls, triangles, quads, sections, visibleSections, queuedUploads and fps for the F3 overlay.
- App wiring (apps/game/**): the game loop, player physics, block break/place through a DDA raycast (raycast.ts), the bridge to client-c's createUi/createAudio, the ?test=1&seed&rd&w&h query handling and the window.__vc harness API the E2E specs consume.

GLSL3 FINDING (root cause of the only red E2E run)
With glslVersion: THREE.GLSL3, three 0.186 injects only the varying/attribute and texture aliases; the 'layout(location = 0) out highp vec4 pc_fragColor' and '#define gl_FragColor pc_fragColor' lines are explicitly skipped on that path (three.module.js around line 6978). A GLSL3 ShaderMaterial must therefore declare its own fragment output. Writing gl_FragColor produced 'ERROR: 0:88: gl_FragColor : undeclared identifier' plus a VALIDATE_STATUS failure, which the zero-console-error assertion correctly caught in all four specs. Fixed in cddd974 by declaring layout(location = 0) out vec4 fragColor and assigning to it.
